passage.full_text:
Paragraph 1 — A town cut off by rivers
In 2015, villages in Nepal have a problem. Rivers separate the villages. There are no bridges. In the rainy season, the rivers are very dangerous. Children cannot go to school. Farmers cannot sell crops at market.

Paragraph 2 — A young engineer has a plan
Prakash is 25 years old. He is an engineer. He decides to build bridges for the villages. He learns how to build simple but strong bridges. He uses local materials. He teaches villagers to build too.

Paragraph 3 — Building the first bridge
In 2016, the village builds the first bridge. 50 people work together. It takes two months. The bridge is simple but beautiful. It is made of wood and rope. When the bridge is done, people dance and sing.

Paragraph 4 — More bridges follow
The news spreads to other villages. They also want bridges. Prakash travels to six more villages. Every village builds a bridge. Young people learn engineering. They help build bridges. The knowledge spreads like water.

Paragraph 5 — Connections and opportunities
Today, eight villages are connected by bridges. Children go to school. Farmers sell crops at market. Young people move to towns for jobs. A mother can visit her daughter more easily. Simple bridges changed everything. Prakash says connection is freedom.
